title: Latency up, nothing changed on our side
source: Live calls to Token Factory (Nemotron-3.5 Lightning) with injected faults

evidence.claim: Baseline and incident windows show identical average input tokens (213), output tokens (48), retries (0), concurrency (1), and app version (v1), but latency p50 rose from 0.38s to 1.79s and p95 from 0.43s to 2.01s.
Stratified by input tokens (0-500) and retries (0-1), median latency rose from 0.38s to 1.79s with no change in request characteristics.
Stratified by input tokens (0-500) and concurrency (0-2), median latency rose from 0.38s to 1.79s with no change in request characteristics.
Stratified by retries (0-1) and concurrency (0-2), median latency rose from 0.38s to 1.79s with no change in request characteristics.

Effect split model on the incident window explains 0.0s of the 1.39s observed latency rise; all factors (prompt_size, retries, concurrency) have varies_in_incident_window=false and identical means across windows, leaving the entire rise unexplained by application-side factors.

rejected_hypotheses.why_rejected: Average input tokens unchanged at 213 in both baseline and incident windows (pack_windows).
Average concurrency unchanged at 1 in both windows; stratified tables show same concurrency bucket (0-2) with latency rise (pack_windows, pack_strat_input_concurrency).

Zero retries in both windows (avg_retries=0, retry distribution 100% at 0 retries) and stratified tables show same retry bucket (0-1) with latency rise (pack_retries_baseline, pack_retries_incident, pack_strat_input_retries).

uncertainties: Provider-side degradation cannot be directly observed from application-side telemetry; could be network, provider infrastructure, or upstream dependency issues.
Small incident sample size (n=12) limits statistical power.
Prompt complexity or other unmeasured request attributes (e.g., specific token patterns) could differ despite same token counts.
recommended_actions: Check provider status page and incident history for reported degradation during the incident window.
Request provider-side latency breakdown (e.g., queue time, model compute time) if available.
Add client-side instrumentation to capture provider-reported latency headers or timestamps.
Implement request timeouts and retry logic with exponential backoff to mitigate future provider-side latency spikes.
Continue monitoring for recurrence and correlate with provider maintenance windows.

result.method: latency ~ the factors that vary inside the incident window, fitted on the incident window only
result.note: A factor with varies_in_incident_window=false changed between the normal period and the incident but cannot be told apart from the other changes in this window; its effect is in 'unexplained_s' if it matters.
